metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Bergen County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Midland Ave & Passaic St Corridor, River Drive & Outwater Lane Waterfront
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 3.415%, with an equalization ratio of 69.8%.
Public education represents 49.2% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 38.6%.
Average residential assessment is $331,550, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,322.43.

neighborhoods.name: Midland Ave & Passaic St Corridor
neighborhoods.character: Dense urban-suburban community known as the 'City of Champions' with two-family homes, three-families, and retail
neighborhoods.description: Vibrant multicultural community along the Passaic River with rail transit at Garfield and Plauderville stations.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Abatement redevelopment along River Drive and high tenant density make property taxes a key pocketbook issue.

neighborhoods.name: River Drive & Outwater Lane Waterfront
neighborhoods.character: Revitalized riverfront district with new residential developments, two-family homes, and community parks
neighborhoods.description: Scenic riverfront corridor benefiting from recent parkland and walking path investments.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Transit-oriented redevelopment providing emerging ratable expansion.

equityAnalysis.summary: Garfield City maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Garfield City, homeowners pay an average of $11,322.43 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 15.64% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 69.8%, assessed values average ~69.8% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 49.2% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 38.6%, and Bergen County claims 12.2%.
